title: Large Language Models for Quantum Code Translation: An Exploratory Study
authors: Xiyuan Li, Yuechen Li, Jianjun Zhao
abstract: Quantum software development is challenged by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented software development kits (SDKs), which complicate cross-SDK code translation and execution. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based approach for translating executable programs between high-level quantum SDKs. We develop a quantum-aware translation workflow whose prompt design and validation reflect quantum semantics and accommodate the version evolution of quantum ecosystems. We conduct a preliminary evaluation of 4 LLM configurations on 43 tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q#. LLMs achieve a zero-shot Pass@1 of up to 72.33%, while one-shot prompting further improves the translation effectiveness. These results suggest potential for quantum code translation by LLMs.
summary: This paper explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the difficult process of translating quantum code between different SDKs. By developing a quantum-aware workflow and testing various LLM prompts, the authors demonstrate promising initial success rates in code translation. This work suggests LLMs could significantly lower the barrier to entry for cross-platform quantum software development.
main_problem: Quantum software development is hindered by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented Software Development Kits (SDKs), making cross-SDK code translation difficult.
main_result: LLMs show potential for quantum code translation, achieving zero-shot Pass@1 up to 72.33%, with one-shot prompting providing substantial improvements.
method: The authors propose and evaluate a quantum-aware translation workflow using LLMs, testing translation of executable programs between SDKs like Qiskit, PennyLane, and Q#.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum computation, specifically translating quantum circuits and programs between different high-level quantum SDKs.
key_observables: Zero-shot and one-shot Pass@1/Pass@3 scores, failure categories (e.g., missing source artifacts, SDK compilation errors), and translation effectiveness.
important_parameters: The benchmark uses 43 tasks across multiple LLM configurations (GPT, DeepSeek, GLM) and target SDKs.
main_assumptions: The study is a pilot evaluation, and future work must address the rapid evolution of quantum programming frameworks and develop semantic preservation metrics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the LLM-based quantum code translation workflow; Figure 2 illustrates the prompt construction process; and subsequent figures/tables compare zero-shot vs. one-shot performance across different models and targets.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the quantum-aware LLM translation workflow and prompt engineering, presents pilot evaluation results across multiple models and tasks, and concludes with future work directions.
why_interesting: While focused on software tools, the underlying challenge of formalizing and translating quantum semantics into executable code is crucial for advancing any physical quantum simulation or hardware control.
